title.value: MICo: Improved representations via sampling-based state similarity for Markov decision processes
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the research paper.
title.quote: We present a new behavioural distance over the state space of a Markov decision process, and demonstrate the use of this distance as an effective means of shaping the learnt representations of deep reinforcement learning agents.

analysis.description: This paper introduces the MICo (Matching under Independent Couplings) distance, a new behavioral distance over the state space of a Markov decision process. It aims to improve the representations of deep reinforcement learning agents by effectively measuring state similarity. The paper provides both theoretical analysis and empirical evidence, showing that this distance, when learned alongside the value function, yields more structured and informative representations. The approach has been tested and shown to enhance performance on benchmarks like the Arcade Learning Environment and the DM-Control suite.

type.justification: The paper discusses both theoretical analyses and empirical evaluations, including comparisons on benchmark suites such as Arcade Learning Environment and DM-Control suite.
type.quote: In addition to providing detailed theoretical analysis, we provide empirical evidence that learning this distance alongside the value function yields structured and informative representations, including strong results on the Arcade Learning Environment benchmark.
